reason: The passage depicts Moses as the central leader figure managing the Israelites' fearful and ungrateful response to the Egyptian pursuit. The text explicitly shows the people's ingratitude: they complain to Moses (וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה) saying they would have preferred to remain enslaved in Egypt rather than die in the wilderness, contradicting their earlier plea for liberation. Moses then responds as a leader addressing the people's complaints and fear, calling them to faith and divine deliverance. The narrative is structured around Moses receiving divine instruction and managing the people's crisis of confidence, establishing him as the leader confronting widespread ingratitude and doubt among those he has led to freedom.
